cases.prompt: Order these four ready todos for today and say what decided the order: pay the September rent, book the dentist, file the WPI reimbursement, reply to the landlord about the deposit.
cases.why: ordering on his behalf comes from dependency paths and dates, and a rating guessed for him is the one thing he has said he does not want

cases.prompt: An email from the WPI registrar with the subject "Spring enrollment" arrives, and what it asks of him is not clear from the body. Write the todo statement it becomes.
cases.why: the capture rules fix the statement for an email whose action is unclear, and that exact wording is the rule firing

cases.prompt: A text message from the climbing team asks whether he is coming Thursday. Capture it as a todo and write its provenance descriptor.
cases.why: no capture rule covers a text message, so the decision is taken and its provenance descriptor says it was a guess

cases.prompt: What is the test command in `cmt/engine/AGENTS.md`?
cases.why: a lookup in a repository rules file is answered out of that file, and what he wants or which area it touches cannot change the answer

cases.prompt: This stack trace came out of the worker overnight. Which function threw?
cases.why: reading a stack trace is a mechanical question about one file, and no line about him helps answer it

cases.prompt: List the fields the `dtsTodos` table declares in convex/schema.ts.
cases.why: a field list is read off the schema, so naming an area or a want of his would be an invention dressed as an answer

cases.prompt: Does the pattern `^[0-9a-f]{7,40}$` match the string `origin/main`?
cases.why: a question with one mechanical answer takes no account of him at all
